claims.claim_text: Two track-search algorithms were developed for the Luminosity Detector (LMD) in PandaRoot: Track Following (TF) and Cellular Automaton (CA).

Track Following is a sequential local approach that builds track seeds from neighboring planes and propagates them layer-by-layer searching within a corridor, whereas Cellular Automaton is a global parallel approach that constructs hit-to-hit segments (cells) across all layers and evolves them into tracks using neighborhood rules.

Cellular Automaton is the default and preferred method for LMD reconstruction, as it is robust against local inefficiencies and handles high-multiplicity events better than Track Following, which can suffer from combinatorial ambiguities in high-rate environments.

claims.claim_text: Two track-search algorithms were developed for the LMD in the PandaRoot framework: Track Following (TF) and Cellular Automaton (CA).

Whereas Track Following operates as a sequential local approach that builds track candidate seeds from hits on neighboring planes and propagates them layer-by-layer searching within a distance corridor, Cellular Automaton operates as a global parallel approach that creates short hit-to-hit segments (cells) across all layers simultaneously and evolves them into continuous tracks using neighborhood rules.

Unlike Track Following, which is effective in low-occupancy conditions but subject to combinatorial ambiguities in high-rate scenarios, Cellular Automaton handles high-multiplicity events better at low beam energies, exhibits robustness against local hit inefficiencies, and serves as the default track-finding algorithm for LMD analysis.
